    "text": "## Body\n\n2.5ex 1.5ex Introduction[]{#introduction label=\"introduction\"}\n\nWe study quantum invariants arising from the infinite dimensional\nrepresentation theory of the quantum group $U_q(sl_2)$. The family of\nfinite dimensional representations of this quantum group at generic $q$\nleads to the sequence of coloured Jones polynomials whereas the\nrepresentations at roots of unity give the sequence of coloured\nAlexander polynomials (or ADO invariants [@ADO]). The asymptotic\nbehaviour of these invariants is subject to important questions in low\ndimensional topology: the Volume Conjecture (Kashaev [@K],[@M2]) and\nGukov-Manolescu's Conjecture ([@GM]) which predict geometric information\nthat is contained in their limit with respect to the colour. Motivated\nby the question of the conjectured geometry contained in these\ninvariants the second author provided a unified topological framework\nthat encodes all coloured Jones and ADO polynomials at bounded colours\nby graded intersections in configuration spaces ([@Cr1], [@Cr2]). They\nlead to universal geometrical invariants for links ([@Cru1], [@Cru2]).\nThese unification results opened up questions about encoding\nnon-semisimple invariants and semi-simple invariants directly from a\nunified perspective. In [@CrG] the author defined a globalisation of\nJones and Alexander invariants by constructing a graded intersection\nthat is taking values in a quotient of a polynomial ring in two\nvariables.\n\n**Main results** In this paper we address this problem at higher\ncolours, and we want to unify coloured Jones and coloured Alexander\ninvariants corresponding to $\\mathcal{N}$ dimensional representations of\n$U_q(sl_2)$. Our strategy is to use quantum groups over two variables\ntogether with their braid group action directly on the infinite\ndimensional representation, which is given by the Verma module. We will\nwork over the Laurent polynomial ring\n$\\mathbb L=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}]$.\n\n**Question:** For a fixed level $\\mathcal{N}$, which is the maximal\nquotient of $\\mathbb L$ in which we can obtain invariants from the\n$\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional part of the $U_q(sl_2)$-Verma module? We start\nfrom the generic braid action on the Verma module and define quantum\ntraces on specialisations of the $\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional part over\ncertain quotient rings. We prove the following:\n\n-  *Level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant at prime levels.* If\n  $\\mathcal{N}$ is prime, then the maximal quotient ring of $\\mathbb L$\n  in which we get invariants from Verma modules is given by the ideal\n  $\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}$ (as in\n  [\\[qideal\\]](#qideal){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"qideal\"},\n  Corollary [9](#coro:prime){reference-type=\"ref\"\n  reference=\"coro:prime\"}). The quantum trace in this quotient leads to\n  a \"Level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant\" (for any level\n  $\\mathcal{N}$):\n  $${\\color{black} \\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}}.$$\n\n-  *Level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant.* If $\\mathcal{N}$ is not\n  prime, then the maximal quotient ring in which we get invariants from\n  Verma modules is given by the ideal\n  $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ (see\n  [\\[idealm\\]](#idealm){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"idealm\"},\n  Theorem [8](#thm:THEOREM){reference-type=\"ref\"\n  reference=\"thm:THEOREM\"}). The intersection form in this quotient\n  leads to a maximal invariant called \"Level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal\n  invariant\":\n  $$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_\\mathcal{N}.$$\n\n-  *Interpolation formula in the level $\\mathcal{N}$ quotient ring.* The\n  level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant $\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$\n  is an interpolation between the coloured Jones and ADO invariants at\n  level $\\mathcal{N}$, which we compute explicitely in Theorem\n  [10](#TINT){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"TINT\"}.\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Quotient rings\n\nLet us fix a natural number $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathbb N$,\n$\\mathcal{N}\\geqslant 2$.\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 1** (Level $\\mathcal{N}$-quotient ideals). We are going to\ndefine two ideals in the ring $\\mathbb L$, and work over the associated\nquotient rings, as follows.\n\n1\\) (Interpolation quotient ideal) Let $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{qideal}\n\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}:=\\left(\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)\\cdot (s^2q^{-2(\\mathcal{N}-1)}-1)\\right)\n\\subseteq \\mathbb L=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}]\n\\end{equation}$$ and refer to it as the \"interpolation quotient ideal\".\n\n2\\) (Maximal quotient ideal) Also, we define $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{idealm}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}:=\\left( \\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2) \\cdot (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\\right)  \\cap \\prod_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2),\\ \\  \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right)\n\\subseteq \\mathbb L=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}]\n\\end{equation}$$ and call it the \"maximal quotient ideal\". Here,\n$\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q)$ is the $\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ cyclotomic\npolynomial.\n:::\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 2** (Quotient rings). We define the following two quotient\nrings of $\\mathbb L$.\n\n1\\) The \"interpolation ring\", given by: $$\\begin{equation}\n{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / \\ \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}.\n\\end{equation}$$ 2) The \"maximal ring\", given by $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{qring}\n\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / \\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}.\n\\end{equation}$$\n:::\n\nNote that there is the natural projection\n$\\pi_{\\mathcal{N}} : \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}} \\to {{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$\nsince\n$\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}\\subset {\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}$,\nand\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}} = {{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ if\n$\\mathcal{N}$ is a prime number.\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Level $\\mathcal{N}$ representation\n\nWe are going to use the $U_q(sl_2)$ Verma module $\\hat{V}$ (defined over\n${\\mathbb L}$), which is generated by an infinite family of vectors\n$\\{v_0, v_1,...\\}$. Using the two variable $R$-matrix associated to this\nquantum group given by\n[\\[eq:Rpositive\\]](#eq:Rpositive){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:Rpositive\"} and\n[\\[eq:Rnegative\\]](#eq:Rnegative){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:Rnegative\"}, we get a braid group action:\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\hat{\\rho}_n: B_n \\rightarrow \\mathrm{Aut}_{U_q(sl_2)}\\left(\\hat{V}^{\\otimes n}\\right).\n\\end{equation}$$ We fix a level $\\mathcal{N}$ and we want to use the\n$\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional ${\\mathbb L}$-submodule generated by the first\n$\\mathcal{N}$ vectors of the Verma module. We refer to this module as\nthe \"$\\mathcal{N}$-finite part from the Verma module\". We introduce the\nfollowing modules.\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 3** (Quotient modules). Let us denote the above\nspecialisations of the $\\mathcal{N}$-finite part from the Verma module\nover the interpolation ring and over the maximal ring respectively:\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\begin{aligned}\n& 1) \\text{ Interpolation module}: \\ \\ \\ \\ \\\nV_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\langle v_{0},...,v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\rangle_{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\subseteq \\hat{V}\\otimes_{{\\mathbb L}}{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}}\\\\\n& 2)  \\text{ Maximal module}: \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\langle v_{0},...,v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\rangle_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\subseteq \\hat{V}\\otimes_{{\\mathbb L}}{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}}.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation}$$\n:::\n\nWe obtain the following.\n\n::: thm\n**Theorem 4** (Action on quotients of specialised Verma module over the\nquotient rings). *The generic braid group action $\\hat{\\rho}_n$ leads to\nbraid group representations on the quotient modules as below:\n$$1) \\ \\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}  :B_n \\rightarrow \\mathrm{Aut}_{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\left( V_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}\\right)$$\n$$2) \\ \\widetilde{\\rho}_{\\mathcal{N},n}  :B_n \\rightarrow \\mathrm{Aut}_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\left( \\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}\\right).$$*\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Unique quantum traces over quotient rings We want to define\nknot invariants from quantum traces that are constructed on the\nendomorphism rings of these modules. First, we will prove that there\nexists a unique quantum trace associated the level $\\mathcal{N}$ maximal\nmodule.\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 5**. A map\n$\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}} : \\mathrm{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes (n+1)})\\to \\mathrm{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n})$\ndefined by\n$$\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(f)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}}\n:=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\ng_j(q, s) \\cdot f_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n,j}}$$\nfor some scalars $g_i(s, q)$ is called a \"quantum partial trace\" if\nthere are two non-zero scalars $a$, $b$ satisfying $$\\begin{equation}\n\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n\\beta_n)) \n=\na \\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n), \n\\quad\n\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n^{-1}\\beta_n) )\n=\na^{-1} \\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)\n\\end{equation}$$ for any braid $\\beta_n \\in B_n$ (see also Notation\n[14](#endcoeff){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"endcoeff\"}).\n:::\n\n::: thm\n**Theorem 6** (Construction of a unique quantum trace over quotient\nrings). *There exists a unique quantum trace, up to a scalar, defined on\nthe tensor powers of the maximal module (Theorem\n[29](#thm:uqtr1){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"thm:uqtr1\"}):\n$$\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}:\\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes (n+1)})\\rightarrow \\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}),$$\nwhere $g_j(q, s) = g_0(q, s) q^{-2j}$ for some non-zero $g_0(q, s)$.*\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Level $\\mathcal{N}$ invariants in quotient rings We are\ngoing to use the above quantum trace, in order to introduce the level\n$\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant of knots. Let\n${g_0}(q, s) = s^{-(\\mathcal{N}-1)}q^{(\\mathcal{N}-1)}$ and\n$$\\operatorname{qt}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}}:=\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\circ \\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes 2}} \\circ \\cdots \\circ \\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes(n-1)}} : \\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n})\\rightarrow \\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}).$$\nLet $K$ be a knot and $\\beta_n$ is a $n$ braid whose closure is isotopic\nto $K$. According to the standard argument to construct a knot invariant\nfrom the quantum $R$ matrix,\n$\\operatorname{qt}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}}(\\rho_{\\mathcal{N}, n}(\\beta_n))$\nis a scalar matrix, and this scalar normalized by the writhe gives a\nknot invariant.\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 7** (Level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant). Let\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\widetilde\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)(q,s)\n:= \ns^{w(\\beta_n)(\\mathcal{N}-1)}q^{-w(\\beta_n){\\mathcal{N}(\\mathcal{N}-1)}} \\cdot \n\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}}\\left( \\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}\n\\right)_{v_0}^{v_0} \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}.\n\\end{equation}$$\n:::\n\nOur main result is that $\\widetilde\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)(q,s)$\nis a universal knot invariant coming from the level $\\mathcal{N}$\nrepresentations of $U_q(sl_2)$.\n\n::: {#thm:THEOREM .thm}\n**Theorem 8** (**Level $\\mathcal{N}$ maximal universal invariant**).\n*For any $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathbb N$, $\\mathcal{N}\\geqslant 2$,\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is the largest quotient of the\npolynomial ring $\\mathbb L$ with the property that the image of the\nquantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant.*\n\n*More precisely, the image of the level $\\mathcal{N}$ quantum trace in\nthis quotient ring\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$\nis a knot invariant. Also, if $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$\nis a quotient of ${\\mathbb L}$ in which\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then\nthe quotient onto $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$ factors\nthrough $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.*\n:::\n\nIf $\\mathcal{N}$ is a prime integer, then\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}} = {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ and\nthis theorem implies the following.\n\n::: {#coro:prime .coro}\n**Corollary 9** (**Level $\\mathcal{N}$ maximal unified invariant at\nprime parameters**). *If $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathbb N$ is prime, the ring\n$\\mathbb L_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring\n${\\mathbb L}$ with the property that the image of the quantum trace in\nthis quotient gives a knot invariant.*\n\n*More precisely, for any $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathcal{N}$,\n$\\mathcal{N}\\geqslant 2$ we have that\n$$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) = \\pi_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$$\nis a well-defined oriented knot invariant. Also, if $\\mathcal{N}$ prime\nand we consider ${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$ a quotient of ${\\mathbb L}$\nin which $\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then the\nquotient onto ${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$ factors through\n${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.*\n:::\n\n<figure data-latex-placement=\"h\">\n<div class=\"center\">\n\n</div>\n<figcaption>Invariants in quotient rings</figcaption>\n</figure>\n\nOur next result aims to answer the question about the nature of the two\ninvariants that we constructed so far. 2.5ex -1.5ex Universal versus\nunified invariants In subsection [\\[rec\\]](#rec){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"rec\"} we study relations between these invariants, and we\nshow in Theorem [39](#JA3){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"JA3\"} that\nthe level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant recovers the level\n$\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant. Then in Theorem\n[37](#JA1){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"JA1\"} and Theorem\n[39](#JA3){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"JA3\"} we show that both level\n$\\mathcal{N}$ universal and unified invariant specialise to the\n$\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Jones and ADO polynomials by change of\ncoefficients.\n\nThen, we show that for any $\\mathcal{N}$ (not necessary a prime number)\nthe level $\\mathcal{N}$ invariant $\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ is an\ninterpolation between the coloured Jones and ADO invariants at level\n$\\mathcal{N}$, as below.\n\n::: {#TINT .thm}\n**Theorem 10** (**Level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant interpolates\ncoloured Jones and ADO invariants**). *We have that\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is a well\ndefined oriented knot invariant and globalises the $\\mathcal{N}^{th}$\ncoloured Jones and coloured Alexander invariants, as follows:\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) = J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q) + \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, s) - \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q^{1-\\mathcal N}).\n\\end{equation}$$*\n:::\n\nAs we have seen above, the level $\\mathcal{N}$ invariant\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ has a clear\nstructure, providing a globalisation that interpolates coloured Jones\nand ADO invariants at level $\\mathcal{N}$.\n\n::: rmk\n**Remark 11** (Rich structure of the level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal\ninvariant). The level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$\nhas a richer structure, belonging to maximal ring which surjects onto\nthe interpolation ring. We have well-defined specialisation maps from\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ to the rings where the\n$\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Jones and ADO invariants belong, so\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ recovers $J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)$\nand $\\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)$ by specialisation of coefficients.\n\nOn the other hand, the maximal ring\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is given by the ideal\n$$\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}=\\left( \\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2) \\cdot (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\\right)  \\cap \\prod_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix} d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right) \\subseteq \\mathbb L.$$\nIf we fix $d \\mid \\mathcal{N}$, the presence of the ideal\n$$\\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}\\right)$$ suggests that\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ is related to ADO invariants\nat level $d$ and an invariant arising from Verma modules at the highest\nweight parameter being the $d^{th}$ root of unity. This shows that this\n$d$-part of the ideal, generated by both terms\n$\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)$ and $\\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}$ has a rich\nstructure which in turn suggests that the invariant itself could encode\ndeeper information than the sequence of coloured Jones and ADO\ninvariants at levels that divide $\\mathcal{N}$.\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Further directions 2.5ex -1.5ex Structure of the level\n$\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant We would like to study the form of the\nmaximal ring at non-prime levels $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$\nand the information encoded in the maximal level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal\ninvariant at\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.\n2.5ex -1.5ex Geometrical Level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant In\n[@Cr2], [@Cr1] the author constructed universal knot invariants and\nunifications of coloured Jones and ADO polynomials using topological\ntools, based on configuration spaces in the punctured disc. The level\n$\\mathcal{N}$ universal and level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant should\nhave purely topological counterparts in that context, given by\nLagrangian intersections in configuration spaces. We are planning to\ninvestigate such models for our future research. 2.5ex -1.5ex Level\n$\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariants for $3$-manifolds This direction\nconcerns the lift of the level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal knot invariants\nto invariants for $3$-manifolds. Coloured Jones and ADO knot invariants\nare building blocks for the Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants\n([@Witt], [@RT]) and the Costantino-Geer-Patureau invariant ([@BCGP])\nrespectively. We plan to investigate the existence of $3$-manifolds\ninvariants at level $\\mathcal{N}$ that unify the\nWitten-Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant and the Costantino-Geer-Patureau\ninvariant. 2.5ex -1.5ex \\*Acknowledgements The first author gratefully\nacknowledges the support of the ANR grant ANR-24-CPJ1-0026-01 at\nUniversité Clermont Auvergne - LMBP. Also, she acknowledges partial\nsupport by grants of the Ministry of Research, Innovation and\nDigitization, CNCS - UEFISCDI, project numbers PN-IV-P2-2.1-TE-2023-2040\nand PN-IV-P1-PCE-2023-2001, within PNCDI IV. The second author\ngratefully acknowledges support by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP23K20214.\n2.5ex 1.5ex Quantum group ${U}_q(sl_2)$ 2.5ex -1.5ex Notations[]{#Not\nlabel=\"Not\"} We will use the following notations for quantum numbers:\n$$\\{ x \\} =q^x-q^{-x}, \\ \\ \\ \\\n [x]_{q}= \\frac{q^x-q^{-x}}{q-q^{-1}}, \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \n [n]_q!=[1]_q \\cdot [2]_q \\cdot \\ldots \\cdot [n]_q,$$\n$${n \\brack j}_q=\\frac{[n]_q!}{[n-j]_q! [j]_q!}.$$\n\n::: {#N:spec .notation}\n**Notation 12**. (Specialisation of coefficients)\\\nLet us consider two rings $R,S$ and a free $R$-module $M$. We suppose\nthat we have a fixed basis $\\mathscr B$ of $M$. We suppose that we have\na specialisation of coefficients that is given by a ring morphism:\n$\\psi: R \\rightarrow S.$ Then, we define the specialisation of $M$ by\nthe change of the coefficients $\\psi$ as the following $S$-module:\n$$M|_{\\psi}:=M \\otimes_{R} S$$ which has the corresponding basis given\nby $$\\mathscr B_{M|_{\\psi}}:=\\mathscr B \\otimes_{R}1 \\in M|_{\\psi}.$$\n:::\n\n::: notation\n**Notation 13** (Rings and quotient rings). We will use the Laurent\npolynomial rings, denoted as below:\n$${\\mathbb L}^{\\mathbb Z}=\\mathbb Z[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}],  \\qquad\n\\mathbb L=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}].$$\n:::\n\n::: {#endcoeff .notation}\n**Notation 14**. (Endomorphism coefficients) Let us consider a set of\nindices $$i_1,...,i_{n} \\in \\{ 0, \\cdots, \\mathcal{N}-1\\}.$$ We define\nthe associated vector:\n$$v_{i_1,...,i_n}:=v_{i_1}\\otimes \\cdots v_{i_n} \\in \\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}.$$\nAlso, for an endomorphism\n$f \\in \\operatorname{End}(V_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n})$ we denote by:\n$$\\begin{equation}\nf_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}}:=\\operatorname{Coeff}(v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}, f(v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n})).\n\\end{equation}$$ Here, for a fixed basis of a module\n$V_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}$ and two basis vectors $v$, $w$ we denote\nby $$\\operatorname{Coeff}(v,w)$$ the coefficient of the vector $v$ in\nthe decomposition of $w$ with respect to the fixed basis.\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Verma module of $U_q(sl_2)$[]{#2 label=\"2\"} Let us fix\n$q, s$ to be parameters and in the next part we are going to work over\nthe ring ${\\mathbb L}$. We will use the version of the quantum group\n$U_q(sl_2)$ with divided powers, as presented in [@JK].\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 15** (Quantum group over two variables). Let $U_q(sl_2)$ be\nthe algebra over ${\\mathbb L}$ that is generated by the sequence of\nelements $\\{ E,\\, F^{(n)}, \\,K^{\\pm1} \\mid n \\in \\mathbb N\\}$ subject to\nthe following relations: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\begin{aligned}\n&KK^{-1}=K^{-1}K=1; \\ \\ \\ KE=q^2EK; \\ \\ \\ KF^{(n)}=q^{-2n} F^{(n)}K;\\\\\n&F^{(n)}F^{(m)}= {n+m \\brack n}_{q} F^{(n+m)};\\\\\n&[E,F^{(n+1)}]=F^{(n)}(q^{-n}K-q^{n}K^{-1}).\n\\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation*}$$\n:::\n\nThen $U_q(sl_2)$ has a structure of a Hopf algebra (as in [@JK]).\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 16** (Verma module). We define $\\hat{V}$ to be the\n${\\mathbb L}$-module that is generated by a sequence of vectors that we\ndenote as $\\{v_0, v_1,...\\}$. Then, we consider the following\n$U_q(sl_2)$ action on this module $\\hat{V}$ (see [@JK]):\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n%\\label{action}  \n\\begin{cases}\nKv_i=sq^{-2i}v_i,\\\\\nEv_i=v_{i-1},\\\\\n\\displaystyle F^{(n)}v_i = {n+i \\brack i}_q \\prod _{k=0}^{n-1} (sq^{-k-i}-s^{-1} q^{k+i}) v_{i+n}.\n\\end{cases}\n\\end{equation*}$$\n:::\n\nFurther, using the structure of the Hopf algebra, we have a braiding\nthat leads to the following $R$-matrix.\n\n::: {#R:R .prop}\n**Proposition 17** (Generic R-matrix action ([@JK])). *We have the\nfollowing action on the basis of the tensor power\n$\\hat{V}\\otimes \\hat{V}$: $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:Rpositive}\nR(v_i\\otimes v_j)= s^{-(i+j)} \\sum_{n=0}^{i} q^{2(i-n)(j+n)}q^{\\frac{n(n-1)}{2}} {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\ v_{j+n}\\otimes v_{i-n}\n\\end{equation}$$ $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:Rnegative}\n R^{-1}(v_i\\otimes v_j)= s^{(i+j)} \\sum_{n=0}^{j} (-1)^{n}q^{-2ij}q^{-\\frac{n(n-1)}{2}} {n+i \\brack i}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-i-k}-s^{-1}q^{k+i}) \\ v_{j-n}\\otimes v_{i+n}.\n\\end{equation}$$ Then, this will lead to a braid group representation,\nwhich we denote as follows: $$\\begin{equation}\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\hat{\\rho}_n: B_n \\rightarrow \\mathrm{Aut}_{U_q(sl_2)}\\left(\\hat{V}^{\\otimes n}\\right), \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\\\\n\\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\sigma _i^{\\pm 1}\\mapsto Id_V^{\\otimes (i-1)}\\otimes  R^{\\pm 1}  \\otimes Id_V^{\\otimes (n-i-1)}.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\label{eq:action}\n\\end{equation}$$*\n:::\n\n2.5ex 1.5ex Maximal quotient rings In this section, we introduce various\nexpressions of the ideal $\\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ in\n${\\mathbb L}$ to define the maximal quotient ring\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$. 2.5ex -1.5ex Defining ideals\n\n::: {#def:condition .defn}\n**Definition 18** (Condition ideal). Let us consider the following\nideals in $\\mathbb L$: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\mathcal{J}_{\\mathcal{N},k}:=\\left( \\varphi_k(q^2),\\  \\ \\prod_{i=0}^{k-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\right)\n\\end{equation*}$$ for $k| \\mathcal{N}$, $k \\neq 1$, $2$,\n$\\mathcal{N}-1$, $\\mathcal{N}$ where $\\varphi_k$ is the $k^{th}$\ncyclotomic polynomial, and $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}= \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}\\cap\\!\\!\\!\\! \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\nd | \\mathcal{N}\\\\[-1pt]\nd\\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\n\\end{matrix}$}} \\mathcal{J}_{\\mathcal{N},d},\n\\end{equation*}$$ where\n$\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}= \\Big( \\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)\\cdot (s^2q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2}-1) \\Big)$\ngiven by [\\[qideal\\]](#qideal){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"qideal\"}. We call $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}$ the\n\"condition ideal\".\n:::\n\n::: {#def:maximal .defn}\n**Definition 19** (Maximal quotient ideal). Let us consider as well the\nideal $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{idealb}\n\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\sum_{\\substack{i,j=0 \\\\ j+n\\geqslant\\mathcal{N},0\\leqslant n\\leqslant i}}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n \\left( {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right) \\subseteq \\mathbb L_{\\mathcal{N}}\n\\end{equation}$$ and call it the \"maximal quotient ideal\".\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Coincidence of defining ideals We show that the three\nideals $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$,\n$\\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ and $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}$\nare equal.\n\n::: {#prop:EQ .prop}\n**Proposition 20** (Structural inclusion of condition ideals). *The\nabove three mentioned structural ideals coincide and they also coincide\nwith $\\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}$, i.e. $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:EQ}\n\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}} = \\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}.\n\\end{equation}$$*\n:::\n\nThe proof of this proposition is given in Appendix\n[\\[Ap\\]](#Ap){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"Ap\"}.\n\n::: coro\n**Corollary 21**. *If $\\mathcal{N}$ is prime, then $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:EQp}\n\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}}  = \\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}= \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}.\n\\end{equation}$$*\n:::\n\n::: rmk\n**Remark 22**. The equality [\\[eq:EQ\\]](#eq:EQ){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:EQ\"} holds when working over rational coefficients, this\nis not true if the ground ring is $\\mathbb{Z}[q^{\\pm1}, s^{\\pm1}]$\ninstead of $\\mathbb L=\\mathbb{Q}[q^{\\pm1}, s^{\\pm1}]$. On the other\nhand, the equality [\\[eq:EQp\\]](#eq:EQp){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:EQp\"} also holds over the ground ring\n$\\mathbb{Z}[q^{\\pm1}, s^{\\pm1}]$.\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Maximal quotient ring at level $\\mathcal{N}$\n\n::: {#def:ring .defn}\n**Definition 23** (Quotient ring at non prime levels). Let us consider\nthe following quotient ring, and call it \"maximal quotient ring\":\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / \n{\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}}=\n\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / \n{\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}}.\n\\end{equation*}$$\n:::\n\n::: rmk\n**Remark 24**. If $\\mathcal{N}$ is prime, then\n$$\\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}= {\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}= {\\mathbb L}/\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}.$$\n:::\n\n2.5ex 1.5ex Level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant Our aim is to obtain\nknot invariants at level $\\mathcal{N}$, in this case for any natural\nnumber $\\mathcal{N}$ (not necessary prime as in the previous sections).\nIn the following sections we will see that if $\\mathcal{N}$ is not\nprime, we are able to obtain invariants in rings that are higher than\nthe ring that we have defined for the prime case, which is\n${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.\n\nWe do so by looking at the $\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional submodule arising\nfrom the generic Verma module, when specialised over this higher order\nquotient ring.\n\n::: {#mod2 .notation}\n**Notation 25**. ($\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional submodule over the quotient\nring)Let us consider the specialisation the $\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional\nsubmodule in the Verma module $V_{\\mathcal{N}}$ specialised over the\nlevel $\\mathcal{N}$ quotient ring as below:\n$$\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\langle v_{0},...,v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\rangle_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\subseteq \\hat{V}\\mid_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}}.$$\n:::\n\nOur aim is to show that we can obtain knot invariants in\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$. In order to do so we are going\nto use braid group actions on tensor powers of\n$\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}$. 2.5ex -1.5ex Braid action over the\nquotient ring[]{#action2 label=\"action2\"} First we will see that the\nspecialised $R$-matrix at these higher rings leads to a well defined\naction onto $\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}$.\n\n::: prop\n**Proposition 26** (Action on the higher level $\\mathcal{N}$ module over\nthe quotient ring). *The action $\\hat{\\rho}_n$ given by\n[\\[eq:action\\]](#eq:action){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:action\"} specialized to the level $\\mathcal{N}$ quotient\nring $\\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$ leads to a well defined induced\nbraid group action:\n$$\\widetilde{\\rho}_{\\mathcal{N},n}  :B_n \\rightarrow \\mathrm{Aut}_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\left( \\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}\\right).$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* The condition that we want to prove is that the action\n$\\widetilde{\\rho}_{\\mathcal{N},n}$ on\n$\\hat{V}\\mid_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}$\npreserves the vector subspace $\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}$.\nFollowing the definition of the action $\\hat{\\rho}_{n}$, it is enough\nprove that the action of $R$ preserves the vector subspace\n${\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes 2}}$. We will show the following\nproperty:\n$$R\\mid_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}}(v_i\\otimes v_j) \\in \\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes 2},  \\ \\ \\ \\forall i,j \\in \\{0,...,\\mathcal{N}-1\\}.$$\nLet $i,j \\in \\{0,...,\\mathcal{N}-1\\}$. The $R$-matrix action is given by\n[\\[eq:Rpositive\\]](#eq:Rpositive){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:Rpositive\"} as follows: $$\\begin{equation*}\nR(v_i\\otimes v_j)= s^{-(i+j)} \\sum_{n=0}^{i} q^{2(i-n)(j+n)}q^{\\frac{n(n-1)}{2}} {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\ v_{j+n}\\otimes v_{i-n}.\n\\end{equation*}$$ We recall that we work over the quotient ring\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}=\n\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / {\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}}$,\nand this is identified with $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}=\n\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / {\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}}$ using\nDefinition [23](#def:ring){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"def:ring\"}.\nLet us also recall the definition of the ideal $\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}$\nfrom relation [\\[idealb\\]](#idealb){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"idealb\"}: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\sum_{\\substack{i,j=0 \\\\ j+n\\geqslant\\mathcal{N},0\\leqslant n\\leqslant i}}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n \\left( {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right) \\subseteq \\mathbb L_{\\mathcal{N}}\n\\end{equation*}$$ Let\n$$\\widetilde{\\pi}: \\mathbb L\\rightarrow \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}=\n\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / {\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}}.$$ be the\ncanonical projection. We are going to prove that for any indices\n$i,j \\leqslant\\mathcal{N}-1 \\text { and } j+n\\geqslant\\mathcal{N}$, we\nhave that: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\pi} \\left( {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right)=0 \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}.\n\\end{equation*}$$ This is equivalent to: $$\\begin{equation*}\n {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\in \\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}\n\\end{equation*}$$ if\n$i,j \\leqslant\\mathcal{N}-1 \\text { and } j+n\\geqslant\\mathcal{N}$,\nwhich holds following the definition of the ideal\n$\\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.\n\nIn turn, this shows that the coefficient of $v_i\\otimes v_j$ in\n$R(v_i\\otimes v_j)$ vanishes if $j+n\\geqslant\\mathcal{N}$. So, the image\nof $R(v_i\\otimes v_j)|_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}}$ is a linear\ncombination of tensors with two components such that their indices are\nall bounded by $\\mathcal{N}-1$. This shows precisely that the action\ncoming from the 2-variable $R$-matrix preserves the module\n$\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes 2}$ (once specialised to the\nquotient $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$) and concludes the\nproof. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rmk\n**Remark 27**. Following the above proof we notice that the subset\n$\\left.\\left<v_0, \\cdots\\!, v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\right>\\right|{\\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}}$\nof $\\hat V\\mid_{\\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}}$ is also invariant\nunder the action of the quantum group $U_q(sl_2)$.\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Unique quantum trace at level $\\mathcal{N}$ We recall that\nour aim is to obtain knot invariants. In order to construct them our\nstrategy will be to make use of the braid group action on tensor powers\nof the generic Verma module defined above. Our construction will be\nsplit into two main parts. So far, we considered a certain quotient ring\nsuch that we have a well defined braid action once we specialise the\nfinite part from the Verma module over this ring. Now, once we have such\nan action, we are going to construct a unique quantum trace, which in\nturn will provide our knot invariants.\n\n::: defn\n**Definition 28**. A quantum partial trace is a map\n$$\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}:\\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes (n+1)})\\rightarrow \\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n})$$\na map which has the form\n$$\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(f)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}}\n:=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\ng_j(q, s) \\cdot f_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n,j}}$$\nand which satisfies $$\\begin{equation}\n\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},{n+1}}(\\sigma_n\\beta_n)) \n=\na \\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n), \\quad\n\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},{n+1}}(\\sigma_n^{-1}\\beta_n) )\n=\na^{-1} \\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)\n\\label{eq:qtcondition}\n\\end{equation}$$ for any $\\beta_n \\in B_n$ and a non-zero element\n$a \\in \\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$.\n:::\n\n::: {#thm:uqtr1 .thm}\n**Theorem 29** (Unique level $\\mathcal{N}$ quantum trace). *There exists\na unique quantum trace\n$\\operatorname{qptr}_{V_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}$, up to a scalar\nmultiple, for the level $\\mathcal{N}$ sequence of braid group\nrepresentations\n$\\{\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}\\mid n \\in \\mathbb N\\}$. In other\nwords, for any choice of a quantum trace associated to\n$\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}$ there is a non-zero element\n$g_0(q, s)\\in {\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$ such that\n$$\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}(f)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}}\n:=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\ng_0(q, s)q^{-2i} \\cdot f_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n,j}}.$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* First of all, it is well-known that if\n$g_j(q, s) = g_0(q, s)q^{-2i}$, then $g_j(q, s)$ satisfies the condition\n[\\[eq:qtcondition\\]](#eq:qtcondition){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:qtcondition\"}.\n\nSo we only have to prove that $g_j(q, s)$ must be $g_0(q, s)q^{-2i}$.\nSince the quantum partial trace of\n$\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n^{\\pm1}\\beta_n)$ is given by\n$$\\begin{multline*}\n\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}\\left(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n^{\\pm1}\\beta_n)\\right)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\left(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n^{\\pm1}\\beta_n)\\right)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n(id^{\\otimes n-1} \\otimes R^{\\pm1})_{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},k,j}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},j_n,j}}\n(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)\\otimes id)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},k,j}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n(R^{\\pm1})_{k,j}^{v_{j_n,j}}\n\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},k}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n(R^{\\pm1})_{v_{j_n,j}}^{v_{j_n,j}}\n\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},j_n}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\left(\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n(R^{\\pm1})_{v_{j_n,j}}^{v_{j_n,j}}\n\\right)\n\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},j_n}},\n\\end{multline*}$$ we only have to show that\n$\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n(R^{\\pm1})_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}$ is a non-zero scalar independent of $i$.\n\nWe see $\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \nR_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}$ to show that $g_j(s, q)$ must be\n$g_0(q,s) q^{-2j}$ by an induction on $M \\in \\{0,\\dots,\\mathcal{N}\\}$.\nTo show $$\\begin{equation*}\ng_i(q,s)=q^{-2i} \\cdot g_0(q,s),\\quad  \\forall \\  0\\leqslant i \\leqslant M,\n\\end{equation*}$$ we use the fact $$\\begin{equation}\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M}q^{-2j} \\cdot \n\\left(R_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\\right)\n=\nq^{-2(M+1)}R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}\n\\label{eq:sum}\n\\end{equation}$$ given in the following Lemma\n[31](#lem:qptr){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"lem:qptr\"}. Now we prove\nthat, if the sum $\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \nR_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}$ is not depend on $i$, then\n$$\\text{P(M):} \\qquad g_j(q, s) = g_0(q, s) q^{-2j}\\quad \n\\text{for $0 \\leqslant j \\leqslant M$}$$ holds by induction on $M$.\n\nFor the case $M=0$, we have $$\\begin{multline*}\n0 = g_0(q,s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{0,0}}^{v_{0,0}} - g_0(q,s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{0,1}}^{v_{0,1}}- g_1(q,s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{1,1}}^{v_{1,1}}\n=\n(g_0(q,s) q^{-2} - g_1(q, s)) R_{v_{1,1}}^{v_{1,1}}\n\\end{multline*}$$ by [\\[eq:sum\\]](#eq:sum){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:sum\"} and we get $g_1(q,s) = q^{-2}$.\n\nAssuming that P(M) is true, then $$\\begin{multline*}\n0 = \\sum_{j=0}^{M}g_j(q, s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M+1}g_j(q, s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\n=\n\\\\\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M}g_0(q, s)q^{-2j} \\cdot \nR_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M}g_0(q, s)q^{-2j} \\cdot \nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\n- g_{M+1}(q, s) R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}\n=\n\\\\\n(g_0(q,s)q^{-2(M+1)} \n- g_{M+1}(q, s) ) R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}.\n\\end{multline*}$$ Hence $g_{M+1}(q, s) = q_0(q, s) q^{-2(M+2)}$ and\nP(M+1) is true.\n\nWe have $$\\sum_{j=0}^{0}g_0(q, s)q^{-2j} \\cdot \nR_{v_{0,j}}^{v_{0,j}}=\ng_0(q,s)R_{v_{0,0}}^{v_{0,0}}\n= g_0(q,s),$$ and $$\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_0(q, s)q^{-2j} \\cdot \n(R^{-1})_{v_{\\mathcal{N}-1,j}}^{v_{\\mathcal{N}-1,j}}\n=\ng_0(q, s){q^{-2(\\mathcal{N}-1)}}(R^{-1})_{v_{\\mathcal{N}-1,\\mathcal{N}-1}}^{v_{\\mathcal{N}-1,\\mathcal{N}-1}}\n=\ns^{2\\mathcal{N}-2}q^{{-2\\mathcal{N}(\\mathcal{N}-1)}}.$$ Therefore, by\nputting\n$g_{0}(q, s) = s^{-\\mathcal{N}+1}q^{{\\mathcal{N}(\\mathcal{N}-1)}}$, we\nget [\\[eq:qtcondition\\]](#eq:qtcondition){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:qtcondition\"} with\n$a = s^{-\\mathcal{N}+1}q^{{\\mathcal{N}(\\mathcal{N}-1)}}$. ◻\n:::\n\n::: rmk\n**Remark 30**. The matrix element $R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}$ is\ninvertible in ${\\mathbb L}$, so we also get\n$g_{M+1}(q, s) = q_0(q, s) q^{-2(M+2)}$ in\n$\\widetilde {\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$ and ${\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$.\n:::\n\n::: {#lem:qptr .lem}\n**Lemma 31**. *The following holds for any\n$M \\in \\{0,\\dots,\\mathcal{N}-2\\}$: $$\\begin{equation}\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M}q^{-2j} \\cdot \n\\left(R_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\\right)\n=\nq^{-2(M+1)}R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}.\n\\label{eq:sum1}\n\\end{equation}$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* Recall that $$R_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}\n=\ns^{-(i+j)}q^{\\frac{(i+j)^2-i+j}{2}}\n{i \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{i-j-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}).$$ Hence we\nhave $$\\begin{multline*}\nR_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n=\ns^{-M}q^{\\frac{M^2-M}{2}}\n{M \\brack 0}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n-\n\\\\\ns^{-(M+1)}q^{\\frac{M^2-M+2M}{2}}\n{M+1 \\brack 0}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{M}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n\\\\\n=\ns^{-M}q^{\\frac{M^2-M}{2}}  \\left(\n1-1+s^{-2}q^{2M}\n\\right)\n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n\\\\\n=\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k}),\n\\end{multline*}$$ $$\\begin{multline*}\nR_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n -\n \\\\\n s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2 + 3M}{2}}\n {M+1 \\brack 1}_q \n  \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n\\left(\n(s-s^{-1})\n -\n\\frac{\\{M+1\\}}{\\{1\\}}\n (sq^{-M}-s^{-1}q^{M})\\right)\n \\prod_{k=1}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n\\times\\hfill\n\\\\\n\\frac{1}{\\{1\\}} \n\\left((q-q^{-1})\n(s-s^{-1})\n -\n(q^{M+1} - q^{-M-1})\n (sq^{-M}-s^{-1}q^{M})\n \\right)\n \\prod_{k=1}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n=\n\\\\\n-s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n\\left(sq^{-M-1} - \ns^{-1}q^{M+1}\n \\right)\n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}),\n\\end{multline*}$$ $$\\begin{multline*}\nR_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} (R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,1}}^{v_{M,1}})\n=\n\\\\\n-s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n\\left(sq^{-M-1} - \ns^{-1}q^{M+1}\n \\right)\n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})\n +\n \\\\\ns^{-M-1}q^{\\frac{M^2+M-2}{2}}\n {M \\brack 1}_q \n  \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})  \n=\n\\\\\n-s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+M-2}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n\\left(q^{M+1}(sq^{-M-1} - \ns^{-1}q^{M+1}\n )\n -\n s\n\\right)\n\\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-3}q^{\\frac{M^2+5M+2}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}),\n\\end{multline*}$$ $$\\begin{multline*}\nR_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} (R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,1}}^{v_{M,1}})\n-\nq^{-4} (R_{v_{M+1,2}}^{v_{M+1,2}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,2}}^{v_{M,2}})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-4}q^{\\frac{M^2+7M+6}{2}} \n {M \\brack 2}_q \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-3}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}),\n\\end{multline*}$$ $$\\begin{multline*}\nR_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} (R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,1}}^{v_{M,1}})\n-\nq^{-4} (R_{v_{M+1,2}}^{v_{M+1,2}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,2}}^{v_{M,2}})\n-\nq^{-6} (R_{v_{M+1,3}}^{v_{M+1,3}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,3}}^{v_{M,3}})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-5}q^{\\frac{M^2+9M+12}{2}} \n {M \\brack 3}_q \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-4}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}).\n\\end{multline*}$$ Following an inductive argument, we deduce this\nproperty for any natural number $M$, $M \\leqslant\\mathcal{N}-2$. Then we\nget $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\sum_{j=0}^M\nq^{-2j}\\left(\nR_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\n\\right)\n=\ns^{-2M-2}q^{\\frac{4M^2+4M}{2}} \n=\nq^{-2M-2}\nR_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}.\n\\end{equation*}$$ ◻\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant For the next part of\nour construction we want to use the uniquely defined quantum traces on\nthese quotient modules together with the induced braid group actions\nthat come from the generic R-matrix in order to obtain knot invariants.\nWe recall that we are working over the following quotient ring defined\nin [\\[qring\\]](#qring){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"qring\"}:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / \\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}.\n\\end{equation*}$$\n\n::: notation\n**Notation 32**. (Partial trace associated to a vector) We extend the\nquantum partial trace $\\operatorname{qptr}$ on\n$\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes 2}$ to\n$\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}$, which is given by:\n$$\\operatorname{qt}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}}:=\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\circ \\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes 2}} \\circ \\cdots \\circ \\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes(n-1)}} : \\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n})\\rightarrow \\operatorname{End}(\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}).$$\nwhere its evaluation on the vector $v_i$ as: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\operatorname{qt}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}}(f)_{v_i}^{v_i}=s^{-(\\mathcal{N}-1)(n-1)}q^{{\\mathcal{N}(\\mathcal{N}-1)}(n-1)}\n\\sum_{j_2, j_3 \\cdots, j_n=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\nq^{-2\\sum_{k=2}^n j_k}  f_{v_{i, j_2, \\cdots  j_n}}^{v_{i, j_2, \\cdots  j_n}}.\n\\end{equation*}$$\n:::\n\n::: {#O .defn}\n**Definition 33**. For $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathbb N$ and for\n$\\beta_n \\in B_n$ let us consider\n$\\widetilde\\Omega(\\beta_n)(q,s) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ obtained\nfrom the above braid action via the quantum partial trace on the first\ncomponent: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)(q,s)\n= \ns^{w(\\beta_n)(\\mathcal{N}-1)}q^{-w(\\beta_n){\\mathcal{N}(\\mathcal{N}-1)}} \\cdot \n\\operatorname{qt}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}}\\left( \\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)\n\\right)_{v_0}^{v_0} \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}.\n\\end{equation*}$$\n:::\n\nThe properties of the quantum partial trace implies Theorem\n[8](#thm:THEOREM){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"thm:THEOREM\"} and\nCorollary [9](#coro:prime){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"coro:prime\"}\nwhich we remind below.\n\n::: {#thm:THEOREMG .thm}\n**Theorem 34** (**Level $\\mathcal{N}$ maximal universal invariant**).\n*For any $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathbb N$, $\\mathcal{N}\\geqslant 2$,\n$\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is the largest quotient of the\npolynomial ring $\\mathbb L$ with the property that the image of the\nquantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant.*\n\n*More precisely, the image of the level $\\mathcal{N}$ quantum trace in\nthis quotient ring\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in \\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$\nis a knot invariant. Also, if $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$\nis a quotient of ${\\mathbb L}$ in which\n$\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then\nthe quotient onto $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$ factors\nthrough $\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#coro:COROLLARY .coro}\n**Corollary 35** (**Level $\\mathcal{N}$ maximal unified invariant at\nprime parameters**). *If $\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathbb N$ is prime, the ring\n$\\mathbb L_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring\n${\\mathbb L}$ with the property that the image of the quantum trace in\nthis quotient gives a knot invariant. More precisely, for any\n$\\mathcal{N}\\in \\mathcal{N}$, $\\mathcal{N}\\geqslant 2$ we have that\n$$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) = \\pi_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$$\nis a well defined oriented knot invariant where $\\pi_\\mathcal{N}$ is the\nnatural projection from $\\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$ to\n${\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$. Also, if $\\mathcal{N}$ prime and we consider\n${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$ a quotient of ${\\mathbb L}$ in which\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(\\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then the quotient\nonto ${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}'$ factors through\n${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#ringz .rmk}\n**Remark 36** (Level $\\mathcal{N}$ invariant over the integers). We\nwould like to remark that all the construction works over the quotient\nring of $\\mathbb Z[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}]$ instead of\n$\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}]$, quotiented by the ideal generated by\nthe same elements. Let\n${\\mathbb L}^{\\mathbb Z}_{\\mathcal{N}} = \\mathbb Z[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}]/\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}$,\nthen we obtain a well-defined knot invariant\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in {\\mathbb L}^{\\mathbb Z}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.\n:::\n\n2.5ex 1.5ex Interpolation formula in the level $\\mathcal{N}$-quotient\nring []{#rec label=\"rec\"} In this section we are going to prove Theorem\n[10](#TINT){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"TINT\"}, which provides a\nformula for the level $\\mathcal{N}$ interpolation invariant. In order to\nprove this, we will first show that both our level $\\mathcal{N}$\ninterpolation and level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariants recover the\ncoloured Jones and ADO invariants. 2.5ex -1.5ex Recovering coloured\nJones and ADO invariants\n\n::: {#JA1 .thm}\n**Theorem 37** (The level $\\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant recovers\ncoloured Jones and ADO invariants). *We have that: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)\\mid_{s = q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}} = J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q), \\qquad\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)\\mid_{q=\\xi_{\\mathcal{N}}}=\\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, s).\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We recall that the invariant $\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ is\nconstructed from the representation theory of $U_q(sl_2)$ over the ring\n${\\mathbb L}$. It uses the induced braid action on the specialisation of\nthe $\\mathcal{N}$-part from the Verma module:\n$$V_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\langle v_{0},...,v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\rangle_{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\subseteq \\hat{V}\\mid_{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}}.$$\nFurther on, if we specialise again at $s = q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}$ , we\nobtain that $V_{\\mathcal{N}}\\mid _{s = q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}}$ is the usual\n$\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional representation of $U_q(sl_2)$ at generic $q$.\nThis shows that :\n$$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)\\mid_{s = q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}} = J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q).$$\nDually, if we consider the specialisation at roots of unity\n$q=\\xi_{\\mathcal{N}}$ we have that\n$V_{\\mathcal{N}}\\mid_{q=\\xi_{\\mathcal{N}}}$ is the is the\n$\\mathcal{N}$-dimensional representation of $U_q(sl_2)$ at generic the\n$2\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ root of unity. This shows that we also have:\n$$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)\\mid_{q-\\xi_{\\mathcal{N}}} = \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, s)$$\nwhich concludes the proof of the statement. ◻\n:::\n\nThere is a natural projection\n$\\pi_\\mathcal{N}: \\widetilde{\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}\\to {\\mathbb L}_\\mathcal{N}$,\nwe have the following.\n\n::: coro\n**Corollary 38** (The level $\\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant recovers\ncoloured Jones and ADO invariants). *We have that: $$\\begin{equation*}\n \\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)\\mid_{s = q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}} \n =\n  J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q), \\qquad\n\\widetilde{\\Omega}_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)\\mid_{q=\\xi_{\\mathcal{N}}}=\\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, s).\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\n2.5ex -1.5ex Interpolation formula Now we are ready to prove Theorem\n[10](#TINT){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"TINT\"}, which recall below.\n\n::: {#JA3 .thm}\n**Theorem 39** (The level $\\mathcal{N}$ intersection form interpolates\ncoloured Jones and ADO invariants). *We have that\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ is a well\ndefined oriented knot invariant and globalises the $\\mathcal{N}^{th}$\ncoloured Jones and coloured Alexander invariants, as follows:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) = J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q) + \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}({L}, s) - \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L, q^{1-\\mathcal N}).\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* The formula for our quotient ring is the following, as defined\nin relation [\\[qring\\]](#qring){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"qring\"}: $$\\begin{equation*}\n{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}] \\ / \\left(\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)\\cdot (s^2q^{-2(\\mathcal{N}-1)}-1)\\right)\n\\subseteq \\mathbb L=\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm2}, s^{\\pm 2}].\n\\end{equation*}$$ We start with the specialization of our intersection\nform at roots of unity, which we know that leads to the\n$\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Alexander polynomial:\n$$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}|_{q = \\xi_{\\mathcal{N}}} = \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s).$$\nSo there exists\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(s, q) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ such\nthat $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s, q) - \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s) = \n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(s, q)\\, \\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q^2).\n\\end{equation*}$$ We recall that $\\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q)$ is the\n$\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial. This means that:\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{r1}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s, q)= \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s) + \n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(s,q)\\, \\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q^2).\n\\end{equation}$$ On the other hand, the specialisation at natural\nparameters gives the $\\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Jones polynomial:\n$$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}},\\, q) = J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q).$$\nThis shows that the following relation holds: $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{r2}\n \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}) + \n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}},q)\\, \\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q^2)=J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q).\n\\end{equation}$$ On the other hand, by the definition of quotient rings\nwe see that there exists\n$\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^J(L)(s, q) \\in {\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ such\nthat: $$\\begin{equation*}\n%\\label{r3}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(s,q)=\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}},q)+\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^J(L)(s, q) \\cdot(s-1^{1-\\mathcal{N}}).\n\\end{equation*}$$ Then, in the quotient ring we have:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(s,q) \\cdot \\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q^2)=\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}},q) \\cdot \\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q)+ \\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^J(L)(s, q).\n\\end{equation*}$$ since\n$\\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q^2)(s-q^{1-\\mathcal{N}})$ becomes zero in\n${\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}$. Combining this property with equation\n[\\[r2\\]](#r2){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"r2\"} we obtain:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\Phi(L)(s,q)\\, \\varphi_{\\mathcal{N}}(q^2)=J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q)- \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}).\n\\end{equation*}$$ This relation together with equation\n[\\[r1\\]](#r1){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"r1\"} show that:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Omega_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s, q)\n=J_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q) +\\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(s)- \\Phi_{\\mathcal{N}}(L)(q^{1-\\mathcal{N}}).\n\\end{equation*}$$ This concludes the interpolation formula presented in\nthe statement. ◻\n:::\n\n2.5ex 1.5ex Appendix[]{#Ap label=\"Ap\"} Here we give the proof of\nPoposition [20](#prop:EQ){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"prop:EQ\"}. We\nfirst prove\n$\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ and\nthen prove\n$\\widetilde\\mathcal{J}_\\mathcal{N}= \\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}$.\n\n::: {#lem:EQ3 .lem}\n**Lemma 40**. *The three structural ideals introduced in Definitions\n[18](#def:condition){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"def:condition\"} and\n[19](#def:maximal){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"def:maximal\"} are\nequal, i.e. $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}}.\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We use the following intermediate ideal $$\\begin{equation*}\n%\\label{eq:INprime}\n\\mathcal{I}'_\\mathcal{N}= \\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-2} \\left( {\\mathcal{N}\\brack k+1}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-1}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\right)\\subseteq \\mathbb L.\n\\end{equation*}$$ We first show that we have the equality\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\prime = \\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$,\nin two parts, as below.\n\n**Step I:\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\prime \\subset \\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$**\n\nEach ideal\n$\\left( {\\mathcal{N}\\brack k+1}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-1}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\right)$\nin $\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$ contains the factor\n$(s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2}-1)$, so $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{r1'}\n\\mathcal{I}^\\prime_\\mathcal{N}= (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2}-1)\\left(\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k+1}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-2}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\Big)\\right).\n\\end{equation}$$ Now we look at the ideal $\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k+1}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-2}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\Big)$.\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{r2'}\n \\begin{aligned} \\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k+1}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-2}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\Big)\n &=\n\\sum_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-1}(s^2q^{-2k-2i+2}-1) \\Big)\n =\\\\\n&=\\sum_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-2}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\Big).\n \\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation}$$ Now, for the term associated to $k=\\mathcal{N}-2$ we\nwrite the quantum number $[\\mathcal{N}]_{q}$ as a product of all\n$\\varphi_d(q^2)$ for $d\\mid \\mathcal{N}, d \\neq 1$, and so we obtain the\nfollowing description of the ideals: $$\\begin{equation*}\n \\begin{aligned}\n&\\Big(\\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1 \\end{matrix}$}} \\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-2}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\Big) \n  =\\\\\n &=\\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1 \\end{matrix}$}} \\left(\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=k}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big)  \\right).\n \\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation*}$$ The cyclotomic plynomial $\\varphi_d(q^2)$ divide\n${\\mathcal{N}\\brack k}_q$ if and only if $k$ is not a multiple of $d$.\nMoreover, $\\varphi_d(q^2)$ and ${\\mathcal{N}\\brack ld}_q$ are mutually\nprime. We also know that $q^{2d}$ is equal to $1$ modulo\n$\\varphi_d(q^2)$. Therefore, we have $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=k}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big)  \n=\n\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{l=1}^{\\mathcal{N}/d-1}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack ld}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=ld}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big).\n\\end{equation*}$$ Replacing $l$ by $\\mathcal{N}/d - l$, we get\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{l=1}^{\\mathcal{N}/d-1}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack ld}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=ld}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big)\n  =\n\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{l=1}^{\\mathcal{N}/d-1}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack ld}_q\\prod_{i=0}^{ld-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big) ,\n\\end{equation*}$$ which is contained in\n$\\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\  \\ \\prod_{i=0}^{d-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\right)$.\nHence, $\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$ is contained in\n$\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}$.\n\n**Step II:\n$\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}\\subseteq \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$**\n\nBy Lemma [41](#lem:qi){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"lem:qi\"} given\nbelow, we have\n${\\mathcal{N}\\brack ld}_q = \\pm{\\mathcal{N}/d \\brack l}_1$, which is a\nnon-zero integer and is invertible in $\\mathbb{Q}$, so we obtain:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{l=1}^{\\mathcal{N}/d-1}\n  \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack ld}_q\\prod_{i=0}^{ld-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big) \n    &=\n \\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n\\sum_{l=1}^{\\mathcal{N}/d-1}\n  \\Big(\\prod_{i=0}^{ld-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big) \n  =\\\\\n  &=\n   \\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n  \\Big(\\prod_{i=0}^{d-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big).\n \\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation*}$$ Then, following relations\n[\\[r1\\'\\]](#r1'){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"r1'\"} and\n[\\[r2\\'\\]](#r2'){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"r2'\"} we have:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\mathcal{I}^\\prime_\\mathcal{N}&= (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2}-1)\\left(\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n \\Big({\\mathcal{N}\\brack k+1}_q \\cdot \\prod_{i=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-k-2}(s^2q^{-2k-2i}-1) \\Big)\\right)=\\\\\n &=(s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2}-1) \\cdot \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1 \\end{matrix}$}} \\Big(\\Big( \\varphi_d(q^2)\\Big) +\n  \\Big(\\prod_{i=0}^{d-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\Big) \\Big).\n \\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation*}$$ On the other hand, let us recall that\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}=   \n\\left((s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1) \\cdot\\left(\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)\\right)\\right) \\cap\n \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2),\\ \\  \\prod_{i=0}^{d-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\right)\n\\end{equation*}$$ The previous relations imply that\n$\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}\\subseteq \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$\nand so we conclude the equality\n$\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime = \\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}$.\n\nNext, we will show that\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\prime = \\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ in two\nsteps.\n\n**Step III:\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\prime \\subset \\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}$**\n\nFor this, we start with the definition of $\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}$:\n$$\\begin{multline*}\n\\mathcal{C}_\\mathcal{N}= \\sum_{\\substack{i,j=0 \\\\ j+n\\geqslant\\mathcal{N},0\\leqslant n\\leqslant i}}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n \\left( {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right) \n \\\\\n =\n \\sum_{i=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n \\sum_{j=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n \\sum_{n=\\mathcal{N}-j}^{i}\n \\left( {n+j \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right) \n \\\\=\n \\sum_{i=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n \\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-2}\n \\sum_{n=\\mathcal{N}-j-1}^{i}\n \\left( {n+j+1 \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+j+1}) \\right).\n\\end{multline*}$$ For $n=\\mathcal{N}-j-1$, $$\\begin{multline*}\n \\left( {n+j+1 \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+j+1}) \\right)  \n =\n \\\\\n  \\left( {\\mathcal{N}\\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-j-2}(sq^{-k-j-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+j+1}) \\right)  \n  =\n  \\\\\n   \\left( {\\mathcal{N}\\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}-j-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right).\n\\end{multline*}$$ Therefore, we obtain that\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\prime \\subset \\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}$.\n\n**Step IV:\n$\\mathcal{C}_{\\mathcal{N}}\\subset \\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}^\\prime$**\n\nFor this last step we are going to show that: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\left( {n+j+1 \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+j+1}) \\right) \n\\in \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime.\n\\end{equation*}$$ Let $l = n+j+1 - \\mathcal{N}$. Then\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\left( {n+j+1 \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+j+1}) \\right)\n=\n\\left( {\\mathcal{N}+l \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$ We show that the above is contained in\n$\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$ by an induction on $l$. If $l=0$, then\nit is contained in $\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$. Now we assume that\n$\\left( {\\mathcal{N}+l \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right) \\in \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$.\nThen $$\\begin{multline*}\n\\left( {\\mathcal{N}+l+1 \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right)\n=\n\\\\\nq^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j}\\left( {\\mathcal{N}+l \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right)\n+\n\\\\\nq^{-j-1}\\left( {\\mathcal{N}+l \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right).\n\\end{multline*}$$ The last two terms are contained in\n$\\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$ and so\n$\\left( {\\mathcal{N}+l+1 \\brack j+1}_q \\prod_{k=1}^{\\mathcal{N}+l-j}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \\right) \\in \\mathcal{I}_\\mathcal{N}^\\prime$. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#lem:qi .lem}\n**Lemma 41**. *If $k$ and $l$ are both multiple of $d$, then\n${k \\brack l}_q$ is equal to ${k/d \\brack l/d}_1$ or\n$-{k/d \\brack l/d}_1$ modulo $\\Phi_d(q^2)$.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* First of all, we have $$[d + k] = -[k] \\mod \\Phi_d(q^2).$$ This\nimplies that $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:quantum integerd}\n\\frac{[ld + d-1][ld+d-2]\\cdots[ld+1]}\n{[d-1][d-2]\\cdots[1]} = (-1)^{l(d-1)}.\n\\end{equation}$$ We also know that $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:quantumintegerquotient}\n\\frac{[kd]}{[d]} = \nq^{(k-1)d} + q^{(k-3)d} + \\cdots + q^{-(k-1)d}\n= \\pm k \\mod \\Phi_d(q^2).\n\\end{equation}$$ Let $k = k'd$ and $l = l'd$, then, by using\n[\\[eq:quantum integerd\\]](#eq:quantum integerd){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:quantum integerd\"} and\n[\\[eq:quantumintegerquotient\\]](#eq:quantumintegerquotient){reference-type=\"eqref\"\nreference=\"eq:quantumintegerquotient\"}, we get $$\\begin{equation*}\n{k'd \\brack l'd}_q \n=\n\\pm \\frac{[k'd][(k'-1)d]\\cdots [(k'-l'+1)d]}\n{[l'd][(l'-1)d]\\cdots[d]}\n=\n\\pm {k' \\brack l'}_1 \\mod \\Phi_d(q^2).\n\\end{equation*}$$ Hence ${k'd \\brack l'd}_q$ is equal to\n$\\pm {k' \\brack l'}_1$ modulo $\\Phi_d(q^2)$. ◻\n:::\n\nTo show that $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}$ and\n$\\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ are equal, we use the following\nlemma.\n\n::: {#strcy .lem}\n**Lemma 42** (Structure of the maximal ideal at non-prime parameters).\n*The ideal $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}$ has the following\nstructure: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}\n=\\left( \\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2) \\cdot (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\\right)  \\cap \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* We recall that $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}\n=\\left( \\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2) \\cdot (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\\right)  \\cap \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\ \\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(s^2q^{-2i}-1)  \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$ In the next part, we are going to prove that:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\left(\\varphi_d(q^2),\\ \\  \\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\right)=\\left(\\varphi_d(q^2),\\ \\  \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$ This relation is ensured if one has:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \\equiv \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}   \\left(\\text{modulo } \\  \\varphi_d(q^2) \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$ Up to a power of $q$, the left hand side term is given\nby $\\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(s^2-q^{2i})$. Now, if we look at the coefficients\nof $s$, we see that up multiples of $q^{2d}$ they are the same as the\ncoefficients of $s$ in $\\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}$, which means that modulo\n$\\varphi_d(q^2)$ the two polynomials are equal. This shows the formula\nfor $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ from the statement. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#lem:idcy .lem}\n**Lemma 43** (Structural theorem of the maximal quotient ideal). *The\nideal $\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}$ is equal to the ideal\n$\\widetilde\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N}}$ given in\n[\\[qideal\\]](#qideal){reference-type=\"eqref\" reference=\"qideal\"}, i.e.\nit can be described via the product of the ideals associated to the set\nof divisors of $\\mathcal{N}$, as below: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}\n=\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{I}}_\\mathcal{N}\n=\\left(\\left(\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)\\right) \\cdot (s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\\right) \\cap \\prod_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\n::::: proof\n*Proof.* We recall the description of the ideal\n$\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}$ from Lemma\n[42](#strcy){reference-type=\"ref\" reference=\"strcy\"}:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\widetilde{\\mathcal{J}}_\\mathcal{N}\n=\\left((s^2 q^{-2\\mathcal{N}+2} - 1) \\cdot\\left(\\varphi_\\mathcal{N}(q^2)\\right)\\right) \\cap \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$ We will show that: $$\\begin{equation*}\n \\prod_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2),\\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right)\n=\n \\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2),\\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right).\n\\end{equation*}$$ For this we are going to use the following criteria\nfor a set of ideals, that ensures that their intersection is the same as\nthe product.\n\n::: lem\n**Lemma 44**. *Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I_1,...,I_n$ a set of\nideals of $R$ such that any $I_i$ and $I_j$ are comaximal, meaning that:\n$$I_i+I_j=R, \\ \\ \\forall 1\\leqslant i<j\\leqslant n.$$ Then we have:\n$$\\begin{equation*}\n\\bigcap_{i=1}^n I_i=\\prod_{i=1}^n I_i.\n\\end{equation*}$$*\n:::\n\nWe are going to use this criteria for our set of ideals. Let us consider\n$d_1\\mid \\mathcal{N}, d_2\\mid \\mathcal{N}$ such that\n$1<d_1<d_2<\\mathcal{N}$. We denote: $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N},d_1}=\\left(\\varphi_{d_1}(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d_1}-1}{s^2-1} )\\right)\\\\\n \\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N},d_2}=\\left(\\varphi_{d_2}(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d_2}-1}{s^2-1} )\\right).\n\\end{aligned}\n\\end{equation*}$$\n\n::: {#comax .lem}\n**Lemma 45**. *If $d_1 \\neq d_2$, then $\\varphi_{d_1}(q^2)$ and\n$\\varphi_{d_2}(q^2)$ are coprime in $\\mathbb Q[q^{\\pm1}]$ and so the\nideals $\\left(\\varphi_{d_1}(q^2)\\right)$ and\n$\\left(\\varphi_{d_2}(q^2)\\right)$ are comaximal.*\n:::\n\nWe remark that this property is not true if we are working over\n$\\mathbb Z[q^{\\pm2}]$, see [@TA] for an explicit example. In turn, this\nmeans that\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N},d_1}=\\left(\\varphi_{d_1}(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d_1}-1}{s^2-1} )\\right)$\nand\n$\\mathcal{I}_{\\mathcal{N},d_2}=\\left(\\varphi_{d_2}(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d_2}-1}{s^2-1} )\\right)$\nare comaximal in $\\mathbb L$. This together with the previous Lemma\nensures that $$\\begin{equation*}\n\\bigcap_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}  \\right)\n=\n  \\prod_{\\text{\\scriptsize$\\begin{matrix}\n d\\mid \\mathcal{N}\\\\ d \\neq 1, \\mathcal{N}\\end{matrix}$}}\n \\left(\\varphi_d(q^2), \\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \\right)\n\\end{equation*}$$ which concludes the proof of this lemma. ◻\n:::::\n\n::: thebibliography\n99\n\nY.         "canonical_tex": "\\begin{aligned}\n& 1) \\text{ Interpolation module}: \\ \\ \\ \\ \\\nV_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\langle v_{0},...,v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\rangle_{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\subseteq \\hat{V}\\otimes_{{\\mathbb L}}{{\\mathbb L}_{\\mathcal{N}}}\\\\\n& 2)  \\text{ Maximal module}: \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\ \\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}:=\\langle v_{0},...,v_{\\mathcal{N}-1}\\rangle_{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}} \\subseteq \\hat{V}\\otimes_{{\\mathbb L}}{\\widetilde{{\\mathbb L}}_{\\mathcal{N}}}.\n\\end{aligned}",

      {
        "canonical_tex": "\\operatorname{qptr}_{\\widetilde{V}_{\\mathcal{N}}^{\\otimes n}}\\left(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n^{\\pm1}\\beta_n)\\right)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \\cdots, j_n}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\left(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\sigma_n^{\\pm1}\\beta_n)\\right)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{i_1,i_2, \\cdots, i_n,j}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n(id^{\\otimes n-1} \\otimes R^{\\pm1})_{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},k,j}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},j_n,j}}\n(\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)\\otimes id)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},k,j}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n\\sum_{k=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}\n(R^{\\pm1})_{k,j}^{v_{j_n,j}}\n\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},k}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n(R^{\\pm1})_{v_{j_n,j}}^{v_{j_n,j}}\n\\widetilde\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},j_n}}\n=\n\\\\\n=\\left(\\sum_{j=0}^{\\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \\cdot \n(R^{\\pm1})_{v_{j_n,j}}^{v_{j_n,j}}\n\\right)\n\\rho_{\\mathcal{N},n}(\\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \\cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \\cdots, j_{n-1},j_n}},",
        "hash": "e8eab5940e8af9af",

        "canonical_tex": "\\sum_{j=0}^{M}q^{-2j} \\cdot \n\\left(R_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\\right)\n=\nq^{-2(M+1)}R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}\n\\label{eq:sum}",

        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "0 = \\sum_{j=0}^{M}g_j(q, s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M+1}g_j(q, s) \\cdot \nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\n=\n\\\\\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M}g_0(q, s)q^{-2j} \\cdot \nR_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\n\\sum_{j=0}^{M}g_0(q, s)q^{-2j} \\cdot \nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\n- g_{M+1}(q, s) R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}\n=\n\\\\\n(g_0(q,s)q^{-2(M+1)} \n- g_{M+1}(q, s) ) R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}.",
        "hash": "1f6cb26d3e21f129",

        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "\\sum_{j=0}^{M}q^{-2j} \\cdot \n\\left(R_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\\right)\n=\nq^{-2(M+1)}R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}}.\n\\label{eq:sum1}",
        "hash": "32cd5c3e38164d60",
        "id": "eq-349",
        "mathml": null,
        "section_id": null,
        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "R_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}\n=\ns^{-(i+j)}q^{\\frac{(i+j)^2-i+j}{2}}\n{i \\brack j}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{i-j-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}).",
        "hash": "3aa4fd810badb5ad",
        "id": "eq-350",
        "mathml": null,
        "section_id": null,
        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "R_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n=\ns^{-M}q^{\\frac{M^2-M}{2}}\n{M \\brack 0}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n-\n\\\\\ns^{-(M+1)}q^{\\frac{M^2-M+2M}{2}}\n{M+1 \\brack 0}_q \\prod_{k=0}^{M}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n\\\\\n=\ns^{-M}q^{\\frac{M^2-M}{2}}  \\left(\n1-1+s^{-2}q^{2M}\n\\right)\n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n\\\\\n=\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k}),",
        "hash": "835d9f7c37da03e2",
        "id": "eq-351",
        "mathml": null,
        "section_id": null,
        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "R_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n -\n \\\\\n s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2 + 3M}{2}}\n {M+1 \\brack 1}_q \n  \\prod_{k=0}^{M-1}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n\\left(\n(s-s^{-1})\n -\n\\frac{\\{M+1\\}}{\\{1\\}}\n (sq^{-M}-s^{-1}q^{M})\\right)\n \\prod_{k=1}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n\\times\\hfill\n\\\\\n\\frac{1}{\\{1\\}} \n\\left((q-q^{-1})\n(s-s^{-1})\n -\n(q^{M+1} - q^{-M-1})\n (sq^{-M}-s^{-1}q^{M})\n \\right)\n \\prod_{k=1}^{M-1}(sq^{-k}-s^{-1}q^{k})\n=\n\\\\\n-s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n\\left(sq^{-M-1} - \ns^{-1}q^{M+1}\n \\right)\n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}),",
        "hash": "fa5004db3514bce5",
        "id": "eq-352",
        "mathml": null,
        "section_id": null,
        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "R_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} (R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,1}}^{v_{M,1}})\n=\n\\\\\n-s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+3M}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n\\left(sq^{-M-1} - \ns^{-1}q^{M+1}\n \\right)\n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})\n +\n \\\\\ns^{-M-1}q^{\\frac{M^2+M-2}{2}}\n {M \\brack 1}_q \n  \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})  \n=\n\\\\\n-s^{-M-2}q^{\\frac{M^2+M-2}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n\\left(q^{M+1}(sq^{-M-1} - \ns^{-1}q^{M+1}\n )\n -\n s\n\\right)\n\\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-3}q^{\\frac{M^2+5M+2}{2}} \n {M \\brack 1}_q \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-2}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}),",
        "hash": "57522d765155a2d0",
        "id": "eq-353",
        "mathml": null,
        "section_id": null,
        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "R_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} (R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,1}}^{v_{M,1}})\n-\nq^{-4} (R_{v_{M+1,2}}^{v_{M+1,2}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,2}}^{v_{M,2}})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-4}q^{\\frac{M^2+7M+6}{2}} \n {M \\brack 2}_q \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-3}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}),",
        "hash": "a949ca07a362e6e1",
        "id": "eq-354",
        "mathml": null,
        "section_id": null,
        "semantic_tag": "other"
      },
      {
        "canonical_tex": "R_{v_{M,0}}^{v_{M,0}}\n-\nR_{v_{M+1,0}}^{v_{M+1,0}}\n-\nq^{-2} (R_{v_{M+1,1}}^{v_{M+1,1}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,1}}^{v_{M,1}})\n-\nq^{-4} (R_{v_{M+1,2}}^{v_{M+1,2}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,2}}^{v_{M,2}})\n-\nq^{-6} (R_{v_{M+1,3}}^{v_{M+1,3}}\n-\nR_{v_{M,3}}^{v_{M,3}})\n=\n\\\\\ns^{-M-5}q^{\\frac{M^2+9M+12}{2}} \n {M \\brack 3}_q \n \\prod_{k=0}^{M-4}(sq^{-k-1}-s^{-1}q^{k+1}).",
